pages.title: Why won't it print? (Not Printable)
pages.text: A $(l)Not Printable$() status means the machine can't print what you gave it, for one of two reasons:$(br)$(li)the block's $(l)material tier is above the machine's tier$() (e.g. netherite on a Tier 3 printer)$(li)the block has $(l)no FU value$() and you're in strict mode ($(l)default$()) — un-priced blocks can't be printed, which closes the "scan something expensive, print it cheap" exploit

pages.title: ...but my structure is mixed
pages.text: For a $(l)structure$() print, the machine doesn't refuse the whole job over a few bad blocks — it $(l)skips$() any block it can't print (too high a tier, or un-priced) and builds everything else.$(br2)Only an $(l)item$() print, or a structure where $(l)nothing$() is printable, shows Not Printable outright. Pack makers can set $(o)unknownBlocksPrintable=true$() to price unknowns instead of skipping them.

pages.title: How do I move where it prints?
pages.text: Use the $(l)X / Y / Z offset$() steppers in the printer GUI. They shift the build area relative to its default position (centered directly above the printer).$(br2)Each axis is capped at $(l)±32$() blocks. That's enough to place a build beside or above the machine without printing into the printer itself.

pages.title: Why did it print immediately? (Auto vs Manual)
pages.text: $(l)Auto$() defaults $(l)OFF$(). With Auto off, loading a disc only arms the printer ($(l)Ready$()) — you must press $(l)Start$() (or pulse redstone) to begin. A manual Start prints $(l)one$() item, or runs one structure job.$(br2)Flip $(l)Auto ON$() and the printer starts the moment a printable disc or item lands, and keeps going. If a print began on its own, Auto is on.

pages.title: How do I get blueprints?
pages.text: Two ways:$(br)$(li)$(l)Scan$() your own builds with the $(item)Structure Scanner$() (right-click two corners, scan with a $(item)Blank Blueprint Disc$() in your off-hand)$(li)$(l)Find$() curated written $(item)Blueprint Discs$() in $(l)village and exploration loot$()$(br2)Server operators can also import $(l).schem$() / $(l).nbt$() files with $(o)/mc3dprint import$().

pages.title: How do upgrades work?
pages.text: Each printer has $(l)upgrade slots equal to its tier$() (T3 = 3, T8 = 8). Drop modules into those slots in the GUI, or Shift+Right Click them onto the machine.$(br2)$(item)Speed$(), $(item)Efficiency$(), $(item)RF Efficiency$(), and $(item)Buffer$() modules stack $(l)multiplicatively$() — two Speed modules give 0.8 × 0.8 = 64% print time. See $(l)Upgrade Modules$() for details.

pages.title: Other Pauses
pages.text: If a print stalls without saying Not Printable, check the status line:$(br)$(li)$(l)No Power$() — feed it more RF$(li)$(l)No Filament$() — dock a fuller / higher-tier spool$(li)$(l)Output Full$() — clear the bottom output$(li)$(l)Obstructed$() — clear the build area (the printer never overwrites blocks)$(br2)Every pause is recoverable — fix the cause and the job resumes where it left off.
